title: Sealed
description:
A `data` field classified as subject-linked, encrypted at publish time with a per-subject data key wrapped by K_tenant_root. On erasure the gateway destroys the data key; the ciphertext remains in the append-only log and is permanently unrecoverable. A reference to this type IS the subject-linked classification marker for a field - there is no separate annotation.

`key_id` is an opaque handle with no derivable relation to the subject. The gateway alone holds the key_id-to-subject mapping. It MUST NOT embed a pseudonym: a sealed blob travels wherever the event travels, and a pid beside the ciphertext it protects defeats the sealing.

Additional authenticated data is the RFC 8785 (JCS) serialisation of {"blumetenant", "id", "path", "type"} where `path` is the JSON Pointer of this field within the event. A blob lifted from one event and pasted into another therefore fails authentication rather than decrypting cleanly into the wrong context.

Decoding yields exactly three outcomes, and SDKs MUST distinguish them: Opened, Shredded (the gateway confirmed key destruction - terminal, drop the record), and Unavailable (the key could not be fetched or the caller is not authorised - transient, nak and retry). Collapsing Shredded and Unavailable makes an authorisation failure look like an erasure. An undecryptable payload is a normal condition, not an error.

alg.description: Content encryption algorithm. Consumers MUST ignore unknown values.

key_id.description: Opaque data key handle. Carries no derivable relation to the subject.

epoch.description: Pseudonym epoch the data key was derived under.

ct.description: Base64 ciphertext with the appended 16-byte GCM authentication tag.

iv.description: Base64 of the 12-byte GCM initialisation vector. Never reused under one key.
